title: Country Living Fair 2026: A Shopper's Guide to Rhinebeck
summary: A Rhinebeck shopping day can end with the right antique, even when it won't fit in your car. Here's how to plan the fair, pickup and delivery.
body_markdown:
The[Country Living Fair](https://countrylivingfairs.com/) ran October 2 through 4, 2026 at the Dutchess County Fairgrounds in Rhinebeck, New York, bringing together more than 275 antiques dealers, artisans and small boutique brands for three days of shopping, workshops, speakers, food and live music.


For a lot of shoppers, the plan is simple: drive to Rhinebeck, spend the day at the fair and head home that evening. That works perfectly until the best thing you find is a cupboard, farm table or antique dresser that has absolutely no intention of fitting in your car.


Fortunately, that's one of the easier parts of the day to plan for. Lugg is an on-demand moving and delivery service that picks up large pieces from wherever you bought them and drives them home the same day. As the fair's official delivery partner, Lugg ran a Large Item Pickup booth on-site, where event porters brought paid purchases from vendor booths, held them while shoppers kept browsing and helped arrange delivery up to 150 miles from the fairgrounds.


Here's what to know before you go, from whether Early Bird is worth it to what to bring and how to get the things you buy home.


## How the 2026 Country Living Fair went


Lugg ran the Large Item Pickup area for all three days of the 2026 fair. Event porters carried paid purchases from vendor booths to the pickup tent, Lugg movers wrapped and tagged each piece, and shoppers kept browsing while their dressers, sideboards, hutches, benches and tables waited for delivery.


> “The Lugg crew really brought it. Our vendors and shoppers were all so impressed and went out of their way to say so.”
> Rachel Barrett, Country Living Fair


The planning guide below was written ahead of the 2026 fair. The dates, hours and ticket prices are 2026's, so check the fair's site for next year's.


## **2026 Country Living Fair at a glance**


**Dates** Friday, October 2 to Sunday, October 4, 2026


**Where** Dutchess County Fairgrounds, Rhinebeck, NY


**Hours** Fri and Sat: Early Bird from 8:30am, general admission 10am to 5pm. Sun: 10am to 4pm


**Parking** Included with your ticket


**Weather** Rain or shine, and most of the shopping is under cover


**Pets** Service animals only


**Vendors** 200+ antiques dealers, artisans and small brands


**Big purchases** On-site shipping services, plus same-day pickup and delivery


## Tickets and planning


Tickets are available as General Admission, Early Bird entry and VIP. Early Bird and VIP ticket holders enter at 8:30 a.m. on Friday and Saturday; VIP also includes premium parking.[Check the current ticket options](https://countrylivingfairs.com/tickets) and[plan your visit](https://countrylivingfairs.com/plan-your-visit) before you head to Rhinebeck.


If you're planning to come back for a second day, check the math first. Single-day General Admission is $28 and the 3-day bundle is $60, so buying two separate days works out cheaper than the bundle. The bundles only pay off if you go all three days. Early Bird is a wash either way: its 2-day pass is $80, and two single days come to the same $80.


## When is the Country Living Fair 2026?


The 2026 Country Living Fair took place **Friday, October 2 through Sunday, October 4** at the Dutchess County Fairgrounds in Rhinebeck, New York. The fair is hosted by[Country Living](https://www.countryliving.com/) and brings together antiques, artisan goods, workshops, speakers, food and music in the Hudson Valley.


Parking is included with admission. The fairgrounds are about two miles outside of Rhinebeck, so walking in from town isn't a realistic plan. The fair is rain or shine, but the Dutchess County Fairgrounds is set up well for bad weather. Most shopping is in covered spaces, workshops are indoors and the music stage is tented. Other than service animals, pets aren't allowed.


This year adds a music stage programmed with The Bluegrass Situation, alongside the hands-on workshops and guest speakers the fair has always run.

## Is Early Bird admission worth it?


**If you're going primarily to shop for one-of-a-kind antiques or furniture, Early Bird is worth it on the Friday or the Saturday, the only two days it runs, because it gets you in 90 minutes before general admission.**


Early Bird entry starts at 8:30 a.m., compared with 10:00 a.m. for general admission. That matters more for one-of-a-kind pieces than it does for smaller goods. A dealer may have multiples of a candle, print or textile. There is only one of that particular painted cupboard.


There's a practical advantage, too: buying something large early gives you the rest of the day to sort out how it's getting home. If you're mainly coming for the atmosphere, workshops, speakers, food and smaller finds, general admission gives you plenty of time to explore.


## What can you buy at the Country Living Fair?


The Country Living Fair mixes antiques dealers with working artisans and small boutique brands, so you'll find everything from things that fit in a tote bag to things that barely fit through a front door.


On the easier-to-carry end, expect finds like textiles, ceramics, jewelry, artwork, vintage pieces, pantry goods, garden items and home decor.


Then there's the furniture. Depending on the vendors, you may come across cupboards, farm tables, dressers, benches, chairs, mirrors, doors, shutters and architectural salvage, alongside newly made furniture from artisan brands.


Those are also the purchases most likely to turn a day of antiquing into a transportation problem. If you're shopping seriously for furniture, bring a tape measure and keep a few measurements from home on your phone. You'll want to know not only whether something fits in your car, but whether it will eventually fit through your front door.


## What should you bring to the Country Living Fair?


The fair itself recommends a roomy shopping tote and fairgrounds-friendly footwear. We'd add a few things if you're planning to shop rather than just browse:


- **A tape measure.** Essential if furniture, mirrors or architectural pieces are on your list.
- **Your car's cargo measurements.** Measure the usable length with the seats down and the width and height of the opening.
- **Measurements from home.** Save the dimensions of any doorways, staircases, elevators or spaces you're shopping for.
- **A roomy tote.** You'll appreciate it by the third booth.
- **Comfortable shoes.** You're covering a fairground, not a store.
- **Weather layers.** The event runs rain or shine.


And maybe a friend with questionable impulse-control advice. Country Living actually recommends that part.


## Can you do the Country Living Fair in one day?


**Yes, but there's enough happening that you shouldn't expect to see absolutely everything.**


The fair runs for three days and includes more than 275 vendors alongside workshops, speakers, music and other activities. The fair itself describes it as a weekend experience and notes that dealers restock each day.


If you're making a day trip, decide what matters most before you arrive. Someone hunting for antique furniture may want to prioritize shopping early and fit workshops around it. Someone coming for a particular speaker or workshop should build the day around that scheduled event.


And if you buy something large early, don't let it end your shopping day. Bring it over to the Lugg Large Item Pickup area and keep shopping.


## What should you do if you buy something too big for your car?


**If a Country Living Fair purchase doesn't fit in your car, you can arrange large-item delivery, use the fair's shipping options or return with a larger vehicle if the seller can hold your purchase.** Which one makes sense depends mostly on the item and where it's going.


### Large-item pickup and delivery


Lugg was the **official delivery partner for the 2026 Country Living Fair** and ran a Large Item Pickup booth on-site. Event porters can bring paid purchases from vendor booths to the pickup area, so you can keep shopping instead of figuring out how to carry a cupboard across the fairgrounds.


If you buy furniture or another oversized item, Lugg can hold it in the Large Item Pickup area while you keep shopping and help you arrange delivery up to 150 miles away, including local Hudson Valley, New York City and Connecticut destinations. Choose the vehicle based on the piece's dimensions and whether it needs to stay enclosed; the Lugg team at the booth can help you think it through.


The easiest process is:


1. Pay the dealer for your purchase.
2. Get the item's height, width, depth and approximate weight.
3. Take a photo and save the dealer or booth information.
4. Visit the Lugg booth or enter your addresses online to see your estimate.
5. Choose the vehicle that fits your purchase.
6. Book the pickup and keep shopping.


You don't need to wait beside the furniture once you've paid for it. Lugg's event porters can carry the item to the Large Item Pickup area, where it can wait while you keep shopping or while the team helps you arrange delivery.


### On-site shipping


Shipping makes more sense for purchases traveling farther away or pieces that require specialty packing or freight. The fair says shipping services will be available on-site, so ask about those options if your purchase isn't a good fit for local delivery.


### Come back with a larger vehicle


This can work if you live nearby and the dealer is willing to hold your purchase. Just ask before you leave. Don't assume a vendor can store a sold piece after the fair is over. And if you're two hours from home, remember that the second round trip has a way of making a bargain antique considerably less of a bargain.


## How far can you have a Country Living Fair purchase delivered?


**Lugg provides large-item delivery up to 150 miles from the Country Living Fair in Rhinebeck.**


That puts the Hudson Valley, New York City, Connecticut and surrounding areas within range, depending on the exact destination.


If delivery is going to determine whether you buy a piece, enter your pickup and delivery addresses to see your estimate before committing, or visit the Lugg booth for help planning the trip. For purchases going beyond the delivery area, ask about the fair's on-site shipping options.


Lugg has handled this setup before. At[Sylvie's antique estate sale in Newburgh](https://lugg.com/blog/sylvie-estate-sale-delivery) , shoppers arranged same-day delivery of farmhouse tables, sideboards, mirrors and other antique furniture to homes across New York, New Jersey and Connecticut.


## How much does furniture delivery from the Country Living Fair cost?


**Delivery cost depends on the vehicle you choose, where the piece is going and the details of the job. The practical way to plan is to enter your pickup and delivery addresses to see an estimate before you book.**


If you're deciding whether to buy a piece, get your estimate while you're still at the fair. The Lugg team at the Large Item Pickup booth can help you think through the vehicle and destination, or you can check the trip online before you book.


The earlier you check the estimate, the easier it is to make a clear-eyed decision about a piece you love. You can still keep shopping while Lugg holds the paid purchase in the pickup area.


## What should you measure before buying antique furniture?


There are three things worth measuring before you commit: **your car, the furniture and your home.**


### Measure your car


Before heading to Rhinebeck, measure the longest usable cargo space with your seats folded down, plus the height and width of the narrowest opening. Save the numbers on your phone. That turns "I think it'll fit" into an answer.


### Measure the furniture


Get the height, width and depth of the piece before paying. If it's particularly heavy, ask for an approximate weight. Also ask whether anything can safely come apart. Removable table legs can completely change the transportation problem.


### Measure your home


The furniture has another fit test after it gets off the truck. Measure the doorway, hallway, staircase or elevator the piece has to travel through, particularly if you're buying a tall cabinet, long table or oversized mirror. If you're having it delivered, mention stairs, elevators, long walks from parking and other access details when you book.


## What should you know about buying antique furniture at the fair?


**Inspect the piece, photograph its condition and understand the pickup plan before you pay.**


Antique and vintage furniture comes with history, which is part of the appeal. It can also come with loose joints, old repairs, scratches and quirks that are worth identifying before the piece moves. Take a few photos while you're still with the dealer, including any existing damage.


If someone else will pick it up for you, make sure the dealer knows. Movers can transport a paid purchase, but they can't pay the seller on your behalf.


These same rules apply beyond the fair. Our guide to[getting estate sale furniture home before the pickup deadline](https://lugg.com/blog/how-to-get-estate-sale-furniture-home) goes deeper on inspecting secondhand pieces and coordinating pickup when the buyer and movers aren't there at the same time.


For other vintage and secondhand finds, Lugg also offers[same-day used-item delivery](https://lugg.com/used-item-delivery) .


## Plan for the thing you weren't planning to buy


The Country Living Fair is exactly the sort of place where the best purchase of the day isn't the thing you went looking for.


So do a little homework before you head to Rhinebeck. Measure your car. Save the important dimensions from home. Bring a tape measure. Know your transportation options. Then go enjoy the fair.


If the cupboard fits in your car, perfect. If it doesn't, Lugg's Large Item Pickup booth and event porters can get it from the vendor booth to a safe holding area while you keep shopping, then help arrange[delivery up to 150 miles away](https://lugg.com/new-york-city-ny-used-item-delivery) . Buy the cupboard. Keep shopping. Let the cupboard catch up with you.
